precepts.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
precepts.point: If there is no candy or donuts in the house, a six-year-old cannot get them. Do not offer children a choice between sugar and good food; they will always choose sugar.

note.label: My Temple My Choice

precepts.why:
Ezekiel says the proverb will be used against us: “As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Very rarely do you see a fat mother and a skinny daughter. If the mama is big, the daughter is big, and if there is a son, he is really big too, because what you eat to get there is exactly what the kids have in the house to eat. The kid models himself or herself after the parents. If you are in the house working out, your kids will want to do push-ups and pull-ups and be in the gym with you. If you like to lie on the bed eating ice cream, they will lie in the bed eating ice cream with you. That self-hatred gets passed on, and that is how the cycle continues: grandmama's fat, mama's fat, the kid is fat, and they all give the same excuse, my thyroid, we big boned. Garbage.

So Proverbs gives the command: “Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” It is you that has to shape and mould the trajectory of the kid's life. That goes from teaching them the laws, to showing them what is good to eat and what is not good to eat, to showing them to exercise and to do their studies: train them in the right direction in every aspect.

If there is no candy in the house, can a six-year-old go outside and buy candy? Hell no. If there are no donuts in the house, can a six-year-old go and buy donuts? The kid eats what you feed them. And stop giving your kids choices: put sugary food and good food before a kid and ask what they want, and they will always choose sugar. A kid does not know. When your kid loves a healthy food, give it to them all the time.

If you are big and your kid is big, how will you feel when your young kid needs insulin shots because he is diabetic from being overfed on all kinds of garbage? Where is the love in that? Laziness is why a lot of the time we don't deal with our kids right and we don't deal with ourselves right. If we want to save our kids, it starts with you first: control your eating and exercise, and then you are setting the right example, so that the daughter who is as her mother is trained in the right way.

precepts.text: The iniquity of Sodom: pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, and abomination committed before the Most High.
precepts.point: The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

precepts.why:
What was the cry of Sodom, and what made their sin “very grievous”? Ezekiel lays it out: “Behold, this was the iniquity of thy sister Sodom, pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness was in her and in her daughters, neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy. And they were haughty, and committed abomination before me: therefore I took them away as I saw good.”

Pride, fulness of bread, abundance of idleness, no hand for the poor and needy, haughtiness, and abomination. That is the cry that came up to the Lord before He went down to see it.

The same iniquities fill the land that is spiritually called Sodom today: pride, wealth, idleness from morning to night, and abomination made law. What the Lord took away as He saw good then, He sees again now.

precepts.text: Clothed with broidered work, shod with badgers' skin, decked with gold and silver; Israel prospered into a kingdom and was renowned among the heathen for beauty, perfect through His comeliness.
precepts.point: The Most High is the fashion designer of Israel. He clothed Israel with broidered work, badgers' skin, fine linen and silk, decked His people with ornaments, bracelets, chains, jewels, earrings, and a beautiful crown; Israel prospered into a kingdom, and its renown went forth among the heathen for its beauty, for it was perfect through the comeliness the Most High put upon them. Israel was the standard of beauty and fashion among the nations, and no brand name of today can touch what the Most High designed.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
The garments for the priests were “a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle”, made of “gold, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen.” The Most High is the fashion designer of Israel. Ezekiel shows how he dressed the nation: “I clothed thee also with broidered work, and shod thee with badgers’ skin, and I girded thee about with fine linen, and I covered thee with silk. I decked thee also with ornaments, and I put bracelets upon thy hands, and a chain on thy neck. And I put a jewel on thy forehead, and earrings in thine ears, and a beautiful crown upon thine head.”

“Thus wast thou decked with gold and silver; and thy raiment was of fine linen, and silk, and broidered work; thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil: and thou wast exceeding beautiful, and thou didst prosper into a kingdom. And thy renown went forth among the heathen for thy beauty: for it was perfect through my comeliness, which I had put upon thee, saith the Lord God.”

Israel prospered into a kingdom, and its renown went forth among the heathen for its beauty, because it was perfect through the comeliness the Most High put upon them. Israel was the standard of beauty and fashion among the nations, and no brand name of today can touch what the Most High designed.

precepts.text: Thou hast slain my children and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire; that is what giving seed to Molech means.
precepts.point: The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

note.label: Leviticus 18: After the Doings of Egypt and Canaan Shall Ye Not Do

precepts.why:
Passing seed through the fire to Molech was child sacrifice: the nations slew their newborn children and offered them to that god, and Israel learned it from them. Ezekiel testifies of Jerusalem: “thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured. Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?”

That is what giving seed to Molech means: slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to the fire.

The abortions of today are no different. The Most High is bringing spirits into the earth, and the child is slain so the parents can go on living as they please; that is the same sacrifice unto Molech, and it is wickedness.

precepts.text: As is the mother, so is her daughter; the pattern repeats unless it is broken.
precepts.point: When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
“Behold, every one that useth proverbs shall use this proverb against thee, saying, As is the mother, so is her daughter.” Many daughters go the way of the mother; the pattern repeats unless it is broken.

That is why the father must wake for the daughter, and why Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again, so the land does not fall to whoredom.

precepts.text: Thou hast slain my children to cause them to pass through the fire; that is giving seed unto Molech.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice Ezekiel shows: “thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured.”

“Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?” That is giving seed unto Molech: slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. It defiled His sanctuary and profaned His holy name, and Leviticus 20 appoints death for it.

precepts.text: Paul espoused us to one husband, that he may present us as a chaste virgin to Christ, so we must come out of the other religions and be committed to the law, statutes, and commandments.
precepts.point: She is not even as a harlot who scorns hire, but as a wife that commits adultery, taking strangers instead of her husband, giving gifts to all her lovers and hiring them to come unto her.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
Paul says, “I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” One husband. Israel here is the opposite of a chaste virgin: not even a harlot who scorns hire, but “a wife that committeth adultery, which taketh strangers instead of her husband!”

The Most High asks, “How weak is thine heart”, seeing she does all these things, “the work of an imperious whorish woman”. He gave us everything and we were not satisfied; we chased the philosophies, doctrines and religions of the nations, building an eminent place at the head of every way and a high place in every street. We gave gifts to all our lovers and hired them to come unto us.

Being espoused to one husband means we must come out of the other religions and be committed to the law, statutes and commandments, so that we can be presented as a chaste virgin to Christ.

precepts.text: A nation does not change their gods, which are yet no gods, but our people changed their glory for that which does not profit, showing everything we did never profited us.
precepts.point: She is not even as a harlot who scorns hire, but as a wife that commits adultery, taking strangers instead of her husband, giving gifts to all her lovers and hiring them to come unto her.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
“Hath a nation changed their gods, which are yet no gods? but my people have changed their glory for that which doth not profit.” The heathen do not even change their gods, and their gods are no gods at all. But our people changed their glory, the Most High Himself, for that which does not profit.

That is the contrary thing in Israel's whoredoms. “They give gifts to all whores: but thou givest thy gifts to all thy lovers, and hirest them”, and “no reward is given unto thee”. We paid to go after the philosophies, doctrines and religions of the nations, and got nothing back. Everything we did never profited us.

He gave us everything and we were not satisfied. A weak heart, an imperious whorish woman: a wife who takes strangers instead of her husband, and pays them for it.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not, and that is the compassion we are reading about here.
precepts.point: When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
After everything she has done, the Most High still says, “Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.” Why is she not simply wiped out? “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.”

That is the compassion we are reading about here. His compassions fail not, so the harlot is redeemed. He establishes His covenant with her, she shall know that He is the Lord, and He is pacified toward her for all that she has done.

This everlasting covenant, the new covenant of Hebrews 10 and Jeremiah 31, is made only with His people. The notion that our oppressors, who glorified our fall, get the same reward is absolute foolishness and makes no biblical sense. The mercy is toward the one He has a covenant with from the days of her youth.

precepts.text: In that day He pours the spirit of grace upon the house of David, and every family mourns apart, which is the shame that comes upon us when the remembrance of our wickedness returns.
precepts.point: When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
When He establishes His covenant, “Then thou shalt remember thy ways, and be ashamed”, and “never open thy mouth any more because of thy shame”. Zechariah shows what that day looks like. “In that day” the Most High seeks to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem, and pours “upon the house of David, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplications”.

Then “they shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him, as one mourneth for his only son”. There is “a great mourning in Jerusalem”, and the land mourns “every family apart”: the house of David apart, the house of Nathan apart, the house of Levi apart, the house of Shimei apart, all the families that remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.

That mourning is the shame that comes upon us when the remembrance of our wickedness returns. When He is pacified toward us for all we have done, and we remember our ways, we are confounded and never open our mouth any more. The spirit of grace and the shame come together, on His people, in that day.
